subject: MedBridge residency acceptance criteria & transient processing (failover) plan
messages:
From: Joan Keller <joan.keller@medbridge.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-01-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Residency & failover processing — initial questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Before we move forward with pilot onboarding, our security and privacy team has a few specific questions about Redwood's region-pinning commitments and how temporary cross-region processing is handled for disaster recovery and maintenance windows. High level asks:

1) Residency guarantee: can Redwood commit at the DPA level that MedBridge customer data created/ingested under our account will remain in the EU (or US/APAC if requested) except for transient processing during failover? If so — exact wording your legal/ops teams are comfortable with.

2) Transient processing windows: in an outage/failover scenario, what is the maximum time our data might be processed outside the pinned region? We need an operational maximum (hours) and an example sequence (primary -> burst region -> fallback).

3) Evidence & auditability: will you provide timestamps/audit logs that show when data was processed outside the pinned region and for what reason? Will those logs include affected request ids and model names?

4) KMS and key locality: for hosted accounts, can customers use a customer-managed key (CMK) bound to a specific region? If not, what controls ensure encryption at rest remains in-region?

5) Subprocessors: a complete roster of subprocessors that could process data if failover occurs — especially APAC cloud partners.

I attached our DPA question list (MedBridge_DPA_Qs_v2.pdf) for reference. If easier, we can set a short call to walk through.

Appreciate a clear map of commitments and a short timeline for a written addendum if needed.

Best,
Joan Keller
Head of Security Programs
MedBridge

--
Attachment: MedBridge_DPA_Qs_v2.pdf (1 page)

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Joan — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (Legal/Privacy lead) and Rishi (Infrastructure) to make sure we give operational + legal answers. Initial responses are below; happy to book a 30-min technical + legal session if helpful.

Summary answers (high level):
- Residency guarantee: Redwood supports pinning at the account level. For Hosted accounts we can commit to keeping customer data in-region (EU/US/APAC) under our standard DPA with a residency addendum. The addendum language we typically propose is: "Redwood will store and process Customer Data within the region(s) specified in the Order Form, except for transient processing required for disaster recovery, maintenance, or capacity bursts as described in the Residency Addendum." We will propose exact legal wording for review.

- Transient processing: operationally we treat failover as ephemeral and prefer an explicit operational max. Our standard operational guidance we can commit to in a customer addendum is: up to 72 hours of transient processing outside the pinned region for recovery scenarios, with a best-effort target of 24–48 hours for return to region. Shorter windows (24h) can be negotiated for high-risk customers.

- Evidence: we can provide request-level audit logs showing region of execution, timestamps, model ids, and failover reason codes. Logs are available via the Console (exportable) and we can produce an operational report on request.

- KMS: for Dedicated and Private deployments customers can provide a region-bound CMK. For Hosted we offer customer-managed keys where available; keys are region-scoped where supported by the cloud provider. We'll confirm specifics for APAC regions in our follow-up.

- Subprocessors: we'll provide a subprocessor roster filtered by region and function.

Attachments: redwood_residency_faq.pdf (short FAQ and typical addendum language).

Proposed next step: 30-min call on Tue/Thu to align language and evidence needs. When works for you?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Residency & failover processing — operational details

Hi all — adding some implementation-level detail so MedBridge can assess risk.

Operational model (example):
- Normal: all customer requests execute on region-bound pools (EU-west-1).
- Tiered failover: 1) local region pool (auto-recover), 2) cross-region warm pool (same cloud provider, nearest region), 3) burst to multi-region shared fleet (last resort).

Transient processing windows we observe in practice: most incidents complete within 4–12 hours; the engineered cap we currently document for addenda is 72 hours to accommodate complex DR scenarios. For customers with strict requirements we accept a 24-hour contractual cap with operational playbook changes (pre-warm capacity and runbook signing).

KMS/encryption notes:
- Hosted: customer-managed keys (where enabled) are created in the specified region; data encrypt-at-rest keys are bound to region per cloud provider capability. However, when ephemeral compute spins up in a different region we rotate ephemeral transport-encryption keys; persisted customer data at rest remains encrypted under region-scope keys and we do not re-land data at rest to other regions during transient processing (we stream requests and responses through ephemeral workers).

Auditability: we log request_id, user:tenant, model_id, region_executed, node_id, and a failover_reason code. Exports are CSV/JSON from the Console. For signed addenda we can commit to a monthly failover report and on-demand event reports for incidents impacting residency.

Attachments: ops-runbook-ephemeral-egress.txt (runbook summary).

Happy to walk through an example failover timeline on a call.

—Rishi
Senior SRE, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Kimberly/Rishi — that helps, thank you. A few follow-ups from Legal & Privacy: 

- We need the exact DPA addendum wording (proposed) for our counsel to review. Could you share a draft that includes the 72-hour and an optional 24-hour variant?

- Subprocessor list: please include APAC cloud partners and any managed services that could see payloads during a burst. We will evaluate those against our vendor policy.

- Evidence: the monthly failover report sounds fine. For any incident where processing occurs outside the pinned region we will want request-level CSV for the affected window (request_id, timestamp, region_executed). Will you attach that as part of the incident retrospective?

- DocuSign: if you can prepare an addendum draft we can circulate internally. I attached a short spreadsheet (subprocessor_matrix_request.xlsx) with columns we need.

Assuming we get the addendum text + roster + promise on logs, Legal is comfortable moving to pilot. Would also prefer a short statement that "Redwood will not persist customer data outside the pinned region except where explicitly documented in a documented and logged failover event."

If you have a standard signed addendum we can start from that; otherwise a draft is fine.

Thanks — talk soon.
Joan
